analysis.investment_thesis: BLS International is an asset-light outsourcer handling visa and consular services for embassies — a business with genuine switching costs, government-backed revenue streams, and exceptional capital returns (ROE 34%, ROCE 34%) that is available at only 19x trailing earnings and 15.3x forward earnings. The combination of 37.4% nine-year net profit CAGR and sub-20x P/E is rare and warrants serious attention.
key_strengths: Exceptional capital efficiency: ROCE of 33.6% and ROE of 34.3% sustained in a business that requires minimal fixed assets, the exact hallmark of a compounder
Net profit CAGR of 37.4% over nine years (INR 31 Cr → INR 540 Cr) with operating cash flow of INR 829 Cr in FY2025 — earnings are real and growing fast
Reasonable valuation at 19x P/E and 15.3x forward P/E for a high-ROIC business growing at 37% — this is where price and quality intersect favorably
key_risks: Total assets nearly doubled in FY2025 (INR 1,616 Cr → INR 3,339 Cr) with investing outflows of INR 1,119 Cr — a large undisclosed acquisition creates significant integration and capital allocation risk
Borrowings surged from INR 31 Cr to INR 404 Cr and finance costs jumped 5x (INR 8 Cr → INR 47 Cr) in a single year, introducing leverage into a previously pristine balance sheet
Revenue concentration in government-to-citizen services means contract renewals with individual embassies are periodic risks that could cause lumpy earnings
red_flags: The INR 1,119 Cr investing outflow in FY2025 versus the INR 286 Cr average of prior years signals a transformational acquisition made quickly — these often destroy value, and Munger is deeply wary of empire-building through M&A
DII holding of only 2.92% despite strong operating metrics is unusual and warrants investigation into why domestic institutional investors have not accumulated
analysis.detailed_analysis:
BLS operates in the sweet spot I love: a business where the customer (the embassy) is locked in by contract and political relationship, the end-user (the visa applicant) has no alternative, and the service requires physical infrastructure and regulatory relationships that are extremely hard to replicate. The asset base is minimal — the business earned INR 540 Cr net profit on equity of INR 2,130 Cr, meaning the returns on deployed capital are exceptional. OCF of INR 829 Cr versus net profit of INR 540 Cr (OCF/NI of 1.53x) demonstrates sterling earnings quality with no accounting games.

My primary concern is the FY2025 acquisition that doubled the balance sheet. Good businesses can be ruined by bad acquisitions. Until I understand what was purchased for ~INR 1,000 Cr+ and whether the acquired business earns similar returns on capital, I hold some reservation. However, even accounting for this risk, the underlying business is one of the best quality-to-valuation combinations in this cohort. I would buy on the strength of the operating track record while monitoring integration closely.
